verified_software_facts: Parrot, Owl and Raven load through one CreatureRegistry
Semantic intents compile to creature-specific joint frames
Telemetry and fault injection remain available
Parrot DynamicsSimulator accepts the V1 HardwareBaseline
Per-joint Parrot current endpoints come from selected servo models
All-servo simulated stall reaches 13.6A and crosses the 12A software current threshold
Feetech PING/READ/goal-position packets match official protocol examples
Dynamics Lab HTTP smoke test passes with hardware-grounded Parrot mode
52 of 52 automated Python tests pass from repository root
Nominal hardware-grounded reference behavior reports zero fault episodes
Fault reporting distinguishes rising-edge episodes from active-frame duration
Watchdog loss inhibits motion and latches simulated actuator power off until explicit reset
Corrected safety-validation demo contains exactly three deliberately injected fault episodes and passes all safety-response checks
decisions: Parrot V1 uses smart serial Feetech servos instead of raw PWM servos
Parrot V1 power source is 3S with separate 6V servo and 5V compute rails
Sustained all-servo stall is a fault condition, not a design operating point
Every hardware parameter must retain an evidence classification
Physical motion is blocked until raw actuator zero/direction/limit calibration exists
Physical development begins with a three-actuator neck-yaw/neck-pitch/beak bench rig
Fault dashboards and reports must never present active telemetry-frame duration as an independent fault count
Nominal validation and deliberate fault-injection validation must be reported separately
physical_validation_required: actual joint load and torque margin
smart-bus signal integrity and direction buffer
servo rail eFuse/load switch and independent E-stop
battery sag, thermal behavior and runtime
full mass and center of gravity
true collision geometry and perch stability
actuator backlash, acoustic noise and lifetime
